article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Proprietary K.C. Brains hybrid
Breeder: K.C. Brains Seeds Holland
THC Content: 26%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Skunk, tropical fruit, citrus, sweet herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 6–8 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September
Indoor Yield: Up to 175 grams per plant
Outdoor Yield: Up to 900 grams per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to intermediate

KC 36 is unusual among classic Dutch marijuana strains because its breeder has spent decades doing something the modern cannabis industry rarely tolerates: refusing to reveal the parents. K.C. Brains still describes the cultivar as one of its successful proprietary hybrids while explicitly stating that its origin cannot be disclosed. That secrecy has inevitably encouraged later websites to attach speculative pedigrees to the name, but the plant itself is much better documented than its family tree. Official breeder material describes a short, broad-leaved indoor plant capable of producing very large, crystal-covered flowers in only six to eight weeks, while outdoor examples can reach roughly 1.75 meters and approach 900 grams per plant.

Its sensory and psychoactive character are equally direct. Strong Skunk dominates the aroma by harvest, yet tropical fruit and citrus keep the flower from becoming purely earthy or musky. The high moves rapidly into the body, producing the kind of dense physical relaxation that K.C. Brains warns may leave inexperienced consumers firmly attached to the couch. That combination—short flowering, large production, old-school Skunk flavor, and a powerful body-centered effect—helps explain why KC 36 has remained in the company’s regular and feminized catalogs long after many comparable Dutch hybrids disappeared.
Genetics and Lineage

The most accurate pedigree for KC 36 is simply undisclosed K.C. Brains hybrid genetics. The breeder’s current regular and feminized listings both make the same point: the parent plants are intentionally secret. K.C. Brains does not identify White Widow , Afghani , KC 606, Spanish indica, or any other named cultivar as an official parent on the current breeder page.

That matters because several unofficial lineage lists have circulated alternative formulas over the years. Those claims may reflect old grower knowledge, catalog interpretations, or undocumented breeding information, but none should be elevated above the breeder’s own statement. What can be inferred confidently from the plant is strong indica influence: indoor specimens remain around 75 centimeters, leaves are broad and dark green, flowers become dense and heavily resinous, and the effect is predominantly physical.

The cultivar has also become genetically important within K.C. Brains’ later work. The breeder currently identifies KC 36 as the male parent used with an American O.G. Z female in its newer Z-710 project, demonstrating that KC 36 remains an active breeding tool rather than merely a legacy catalog name. Its continuing use suggests that the company still values the line for vigor, potency, structure, or production even while withholding its original parental formula.
Effects and Experience

Physical impact is the defining feature of the experience. K.C. Brains describes KC 36 as producing a powerful body hit and specifically cautions that inexperienced smokers may find themselves couch-locked. The onset can feel deceptively pleasant, with a warm mental shift and greater ease settling in before the heavier portion becomes obvious.

As the high develops, movement tends to become less appealing. Shoulders loosen, physical tension drops, and ordinary tasks may start requiring more effort than expected. The mental effect is not necessarily blank or immediately sleepy; some consumers may remain conversational or introspective while feeling physically anchored. That split makes the cultivar better suited to relaxed evenings, movies, music, and unstructured social time than to driving, detailed work, or anything requiring fast reactions.

K.C. Brains repeatedly calls the cultivar high in THC but does not publish a fixed laboratory percentage for the original seed line. That restraint is worth preserving. Seed-grown cannabis varies with phenotype, environment, nutrition, harvest timing, and laboratory method, so one modern test should not become a permanent strain statistic. Regardless of the exact number, high-THC marijuana can cause dizziness, short-term memory impairment, anxiety, dry mouth, slowed reaction time, and excessive sedation when consumed beyond personal tolerance.
Medical Benefits

KC 36 has historically been associated with nighttime relaxation because of its heavy body effect. The breeder itself mentions use by people who have difficulty relaxing or sleeping, but that statement should be understood as historical strain positioning rather than clinical evidence. No controlled trial has shown that KC 36 specifically treats insomnia, pain, anxiety, or another medical condition.

Broader cannabis research offers more limited guidance. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health reports evidence of small or modest benefits from cannabis or cannabinoids for some forms of chronic pain, while research involving sleep has produced uncertain results. In people with other health conditions, cannabinoids have sometimes been associated with improved sleep, but researchers cannot always determine whether sleep improves directly or because another symptom becomes less severe.

The cultivar’s strong physical effect can also become a disadvantage. THC-containing weed may cause sleepiness, dizziness, impaired judgment, anxiety, or difficulty concentrating, and cannabinoids can interact with medications. Medical consumers should therefore use current product testing, cautious dosing, and appropriate professional guidance rather than relying solely on KC 36’s reputation as a relaxing strain.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

KC 36 changes noticeably as flowering progresses. The finished product is defined by strong Skunk, but the flavor carries tropical fruit and citrus underneath that heavier odor. K.C. Brains specifically describes the weed as strongly skunky while noting tropical and citrus characteristics in the taste. That contrast prevents the cultivar from tasting like a simple earthy indica.

Earlier in flower, the aromatic profile can seem sweeter and fruitier. As resin accumulates and the flowers mature, the aroma grows darker and more forceful, eventually settling into dense Skunk with a sweet fruit background. Citrus provides a sharper top note, while earth and resin appear toward the finish. The result sits comfortably within classic Dutch cannabis flavor rather than modern pastry, cream, or candy genetics.

No authoritative K.C. Brains terpene panel has been published for the cultivar. Assigning permanent percentages of myrcene, caryophyllene, limonene, or another terpene would therefore create false precision. The breeder-documented sensory profile—Skunk, tropical fruit, and citrus—is more defensible. A controlled dry and cure should preserve those brighter fruit notes, which can otherwise disappear and leave the heavier earthy Skunk component dominating the jar.
Growing Information

Indoors, KC 36 is remarkably compact for its production potential. K.C. Brains lists average height at approximately 75 centimeters and yield up to 175 grams per plant. The cultivar can be grown in either soil or hydroponic systems, and the breeder gives a flowering window of only six to eight weeks. Dark green broad leaves and irregular multi-branch growth give it a distinctly indica-like appearance, while the finished buds become dense and heavily covered in silvery resin.

Outdoor cultivation changes the scale dramatically. Plants can reach around 1.75 meters, with breeder-listed yield potential as high as 900 grams per plant. Outdoor flowering is approximately six to nine weeks, and harvest generally falls between late September and mid-October. Historical K.C. Brains material also describes the cultivar as hardy enough to tolerate periods of rain and cooler weather, making it more forgiving than genetics that demand a long, hot autumn.

Structure deserves attention because plants are described as multi-branched and somewhat irregular rather than perfectly symmetrical. Growers should therefore shape the canopy according to the individual plant instead of forcing every seedling into the same training plan. Dense flowers also require adequate airflow late in bloom. Weather tolerance does not equal immunity to bud rot, and large resinous colas can retain moisture when rain or indoor humidity remains elevated.

Maturity can arrive quickly, particularly indoors, but calendar days should remain a guide rather than the only harvest signal. Trichome development, calyx swelling, aroma, pistil recession, and overall senescence provide a fuller picture. Allowing the flowers to finish properly is especially important with KC 36 because the aroma appears to evolve toward its stronger Skunk character as maturation advances.

Post-harvest treatment should be equally measured. Thick buds require enough drying time for internal moisture to escape evenly. Drying too quickly may preserve weight on paper while sacrificing tropical fruit and citrus complexity. A slower cure allows the intense Skunk character to integrate with the sweeter side instead of overwhelming it.
FAQ
What is the genetics of KC 36?
K.C. Brains deliberately keeps the parents of KC 36 secret. The breeder officially classifies it only as a hybrid and states that its origin cannot be disclosed publicly.
Who bred KC 36?
KC 36 was created by K.C. Brains Seeds Holland, a long-running Dutch cannabis breeding company whose current catalog still includes the strain in both regular and feminized form.
How long does KC 36 take to flower?
Indoor plants generally flower for approximately six to eight weeks. Outdoors, flowering is listed at six to nine weeks, with harvest from the end of September through roughly the middle of October.
What does KC 36 taste like?
The breeder describes a strong Skunk aroma accompanied by tropical fruit and citrus flavors. Earthy, sweet, and resinous notes can become more noticeable as the flowers mature and cure.
How much does KC 36 yield?
K.C. Brains lists indoor yield at up to approximately 175 grams per plant. Outdoor plants can reach approximately 900 grams each under favorable conditions while growing to around 1.75 meters tall.
Final Thoughts on KC 36

KC 36 proves that a cultivar does not need a publicly dissected family tree to develop a durable identity. K.C. Brains has kept its parents secret while continuing to sell the strain for decades, leaving plant performance as the clearest evidence of what the breeding program accomplished. Short indoor stature, broad foliage, dense resinous buds, heavy physical effects, and a six-to-eight-week flowering period all point toward strong indica influence, even though the exact genetic ingredients remain proprietary.

Production is one of its strongest arguments. Indoors, a roughly 75-centimeter plant can produce up to about 175 grams. Outdoors, KC 36 can reach 1.75 meters and potentially approach 900 grams per plant, with harvest arriving from late September into mid-October. That combination of manageable indoor dimensions and substantially greater outdoor performance explains the breeder’s long-standing emphasis on yield per growing area.

Flavor gives this weed strain enough personality to avoid becoming merely a production plant. Strong Skunk dominates the mature flowers, while tropical fruit and citrus add brightness before the smoke settles into earthier resin. Effects follow a heavier trajectory, progressing toward deep physical relaxation and potential couch-lock rather than sustained stimulation.
